questions.stem: During melting, the temperature of a pure substance remains constant even though energy is being supplied. Why?

options.text: The thermometer is not working correctly
All the energy is being used to overcome the forces between particles, not to increase kinetic energy
Energy is being lost to the surroundings at the same rate
The substance has reached its maximum temperature

questions.explanation: During a change of state, the energy supplied is used to overcome the intermolecular forces holding particles together (increasing potential energy), rather than increasing the kinetic energy of the particles. Since temperature is related to kinetic energy, the temperature stays constant until all the substance has changed state.

questions.stem: What is the name for the change of state from gas directly to solid?
questions.explanation: Deposition is the direct change from gas to solid without passing through the liquid state. The reverse process (solid directly to gas) is called sublimation. Condensation is gas to liquid, and freezing is liquid to solid. An everyday example of deposition is frost forming when water vapour in the air changes directly to ice crystals.

questions.stem: A heating curve shows temperature on the y-axis and time on the x-axis. There are two flat sections. What do these flat sections represent?

options.text: No energy is being supplied to the substance
The substance is changing state (melting and boiling)
The substance has reached thermal equilibrium

questions.explanation: On a heating curve, flat (horizontal) sections indicate changes of state. The first flat section is melting (solid to liquid) and the second is boiling (liquid to gas). During these changes, energy is used to overcome intermolecular forces rather than increase temperature. The sloping sections show the substance heating up within one state.

questions.stem: Why is a change of state classified as a physical change rather than a chemical change?

options.text: Because the change is reversible and no new substances are formed
Because it only happens to pure substances

questions.explanation: Changes of state are physical changes because they are reversible (ice can melt and water can freeze again) and no new chemical substances are formed. The particles remain the same substance throughout - only their arrangement, spacing, and energy change. Chemical changes produce new substances and are usually irreversible. Energy IS involved in changes of state.

questions.stem: Iodine can change directly from a solid to a purple gas when heated gently. What is this process called?
questions.explanation: Sublimation is the process where a solid changes directly into a gas without first becoming a liquid. Iodine is a well-known example that sublimes when heated gently, producing a purple vapour. Other examples include dry ice (solid CO₂) and some air fresheners. Decomposition would involve breaking the substance into different chemicals.
